Summary: CF: No-Op Command
Description: When CF receives a "No-Op" command, CF shall increment the "CF Valid-Command Counter" and issue a cFE event message.
Requirement Rationale: CF application is a cFS compliant component that must implement the cFS architectural patterns. The No-Op command allows operational checks on the end-to-end CF command and telemetry paths.

Summary: CF: Reset Counters Command
Description: When a "Reset-Counters" command is received, CF shall set the command-specified "housekeeping counters" to a value of zero.
Requirement Rationale: cFS architectural pattern for application operational interfaces. Allows for partial or full resetting of housekeeping counters. All reset operations should be observable.

Summary: CF: Command Length Verification
Description: If a command's header-specified length is not equal to the expected command length, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, command must be validated prior to execution. Basic command verification in the event of SEU or memory corruption.

Summary: CF: Valid Command Counter
Description: When CF receives a valid command, CF shall increment the "CF Valid-Command Counter" and issue a "Command Received" cFE event message.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Reject Invalid Command
Description: When CF receives a command, if the command is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, invalid commands must be rejected and not executed.

Summary: CF: Reject Invalid Command - Validation Before Execution
Description: When CF receives a command, CF shall check that the command is valid before execution.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, commands and their parameters must be validated prior to execution

Summary: CF: Reject Invalid Command - Event And Counter
Description: When CF rejects a command, CF shall issue a "Command Rejected" error event message and increment the "CF Command Rejected" Counter.
Requirement Rationale: Provide operator feedback; operators need to be made aware of command rejection both in real-time through cFS event messages and through HouseKeeping telemetry through counters.

Summary: CF: Process Received File Transfer
Description: When CF receives a CFDP receive-file protocol-directive PDU, CF shall process the file transfer request according to the directive-specified CFDP Mode, "Unacknowledged" Class-1 Service or "Acknowledged" Class-2 Service.
Requirement Rationale: Basic file transfer function that specifies the CFDP classes that shall be implemented.

Summary: CF: Extract PDUs From Software Bus Messages
Description: CF shall extract uplinked CFDP PDUs from cFE-SB messages.
Requirement Rationale: CF application is a cFS compliant component that must implement the cFS architectural patterns

Summary: CF: Reconstruct Received File
Description: CF shall extract file data from File-Data PDUs and reconstruct an identical copy of the extracted file from the meta-data-specified directory.
Requirement Rationale: Basic CFDP function with fault handling defined in sub requirements

Summary: CF: Reconstruct Received File - Fault Handling
Description: If CF detects that a "fault" has occurred, CF shall close out the transaction and issue an "Error" cFE event message.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, errors in execution must be detected and handled with appropriate constraints on resource use and state machine iterations.  "Close out" is intentionally vague since the action needs to be appropriate for the transmission class.  As long as the transaction doesn't hang and become stale the requirement is met.  Note "cancel" is overly specific, there's a cancel transaction command that is different than what is done here.

Summary: CF: Reconstruct Received File - Fault Handling - Detected Fault Scenarios
Description:
CF shall detect the following scenarios and identify them as faults:
1. Positive Ack Limit Reached
2. Filestore Rejection
3. File-CRC Mismatch Failure
4. File-Size Error
5. NAK Limit Reached
6. Inactivity Limit Reached
Requirement Rationale: Fault scenarios explicitly listed and tested for specification compliance.

Summary: CF: Reconstruct Received File - Fault Handling - Reset Of Freed Transaction
Description: CF shall issue a DEBUG message if an attempt is made to reset a transaction that has already been freed
Requirement Rationale: Provides diagnostic visibility into invalid or duplicate transaction cleanup attempts

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, CF shall play back the file indicated by the command-specified: filename, source path, destination path, keep/delete flag, service class, priority, channel, and peer-entity id.
Requirement Rationale: Also referred to as "playback file" command. Basic function of file transfer required to operate cFS flight systems.

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command - File Open
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, if the command-specified is open, CF reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Open files are in a uncertain state and may change during transfer potential containing erroneous data or cause other undefined behaviors

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command - File Not Found
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, if the command-specified file is not found, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, command must be validated prior to execution. Provides operational interface as to why the command was not executed.

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command - Pending Queue Full
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, if the playback-pending queue is full, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, command must be validated prior to execution. Provides operational interface as to why the command was not executed. Filterable is required to avoid multiple events when commands are sequenced.

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command - Invalid Channel
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, if the command-specified playback-channel number is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, command must be validated prior to execution

Summary: CF: Transfer File Command - Invalid Service Class
Description: When CF receives a "Transfer File" command, if the command-specified CFDP class is neither Class 1 nor Class 2, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: CF App only supports Class 1 and Class 2 CFDP requests

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command
Description: When CF receives a "Playback Directory" command, CF shall play back all the files inside the command-specified directory as indicated by the command-specified service class, priority, destination path, keep/delete flag, channel, and peer-entity id.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to support automation of file transfer. Interface excludes subdirectories to reduce complexity of implementation. Note the

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command - Skip Open File
Description: While CF is playing back multiple files, if the next file to be transferred is open, CF shall skip its transfer and issue an error event message.
Requirement Rationale: Open files are in a uncertain state and may change during transfer potential containing erroneous data.  Note this requirement is different than CF3000.1 in that this is determined at time of playback not at command receipt.

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command - Directory Not Found
Description: When CF receives a "Playback Directory" command, if the command-specified directory is not found, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, command must be validated prior to execution. Provides operational interface as to why the command was not executed.

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command - Pending Queue Full
Description: When CF receives a "Playback Directory" command, if the playback-pending queue is full, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: For robust and secure operations, constraints on resource violations must be checked and reported.

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command - Invalid Channel
Description: When CF receives a "Playback Directory" command, if the command-specified playback channel number is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback when commands are malformed.

Summary: CF: Playback Directory Command - Invalid Service Class
Description: When CF receives a "Playback Directory" command, if the command-specified class number is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Basic requirement to check parameters for reliable and secure operations.

Summary: CF: Publish PDUs To Software Bus
Description: CF shall encapsulate and publish CFDP-PDUs as cFE-SB messages.
Requirement Rationale: CF application is a cFS compliant component that must implement the cFS architectural patterns. Each channel's MID should be unique to that channel. The intent is to allow different communication interfaces to subscribe to a selected channel and manage it independently

Summary: CF: Publish PDUs To Software Bus - Unique Message ID Per Channel
Description: Each CF channel shall have a unique cFE-SB Message ID.
Requirement Rationale: Playback channels may have different message routes to destination. In cFS, the Message ID provides that routing identifier. Unique cFE-SB Message IDs can avoid data corruption and memory problems.

Summary: CF: Publish PDUs To Software Bus - Unique Message ID Per Channel - Configuration Table
Description: The CF-channel cFE-SB Message IDs shall be specified in a CF configuration table.
Requirement Rationale: Run-time configuration table supports ease of deployment, operation maintenance, fault management, and data path configuration.

Summary: CF: External PDU Output Rate Control
Description: The PDU output rate shall be controllable from outside the CF Application.
Requirement Rationale: As a data source in a real-time resourced constrained system, CF must not send more data than the receiver can reliably process or forward

Summary: CF: Sequential Playback Within A Channel
Description: While there are multiple transactions in the playback-pending queue for a given channel, CF shall wait for the "EOF Sent" marker on the file currently being played back before starting playback for the next file in the queue.
Requirement Rationale:
Provides predictable file-in-order delivery. This does not imply that the "EOF Sent" has been acknowledged by the receiving peer entity.

Although CCSDS 3.1.2 says "The CFDP entity shall be implemented such that virtually any number of transactions may be concurrently in various stages of transmission or reception at a single CFDP entity." this number must be constrained for performance.

Summary: CF: Pending Queue Check Frequency
Description: While there is no playback in progress, CF shall check the playback-pending channel queue for files at the configuration-table-defied frequency.
Requirement Rationale: Supports automation of playback queuing

Summary: CF: Configurable Pending Queue Depth
Description: The CF channel playback-pending-queue depth shall be configurable.
Requirement Rationale: Supports recovery of file transfer operations to a known configuration and state

Summary: CF: Configurable History Queue Depth
Description: The CF file-transfer history-queue depth shall be configurable.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to support user knowledge of which files have been transferred and in what order.

Summary: CF: Configurable Number Of Channels
Description: The number of CF channels shall be defined by a CF configuration table.
Requirement Rationale: Table-defined configurations support cFS architecture goals of scalability and reconfiguration of mission variability points

Summary: CF: Configurable Channel Parameters
Description: CF-channel parameters shall be defined by a CF configuration table.
Requirement Rationale: Table-defined configurations support cFS architecture goals of scalability and reconfiguration of mission variability points

Summary: CF: Configurable Channel Parameters - Configuration Table Contents
Description:
The "CF Configuration Table" shall include the following parameters:
-- Engine parameter(s)
1. Local entity ID
-- Channel parameters (per-channel)
2. Dequeue Enable 
3. Transmit PDU MID
4. Receive PDU MID
5. Handshake Semaphore Name
6. Acknowledge timer limit
7. Non-acknowledge timer limit
8. Acknowledge retry limit
9. Non-acknowledge retry limit
10. Inactivity timer limit
-- Polling Directory Parameters (per-polling directory)
11. Enable State
12. CFDP Class
13. Priority
14. Source Path
15. Destination Path
16. Peer Entity Id
Requirement Rationale: Engine, channel, and polling directory configuration parameters for operational flexibility.

Summary: CF: Dedicated Channel Pending Queue
Description: Each CF channel shall have a dedicated and independent pending queue.
Requirement Rationale:
Playback channels should be independent to avoid one channels from stalling another channel.

The channel dictates the SB MsgId / Apid that the playback data PDUs will be generated with. Separate queues also helps when the one channel is throttled - e.g. if there are two channels and one is slow and one is faster, a playback requests to the slow channel may block the faster channel if they shared a single pending queue.

Summary: CF: Enable Directory Polling Command
Description: When CF receives an "Enable Polling" command, CF shall enable poll-directory processing.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface

Summary: CF: Polling Directory Scan Frequency
Description: CF Polling Directories shall be polled for files at the configuration-table-defined frequency.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to support optimization of resource utilization and file transfer bandwidth

Summary: CF: Polling Directory Transmission Priority
Description: CF shall send all files in the polling directory at the configuration-table-specified priority level.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface for resource management

Summary: CF: Disable Directory Polling Command
Description: When CF receives a "Disable Polling" command, CF shall disable poll-directory processing.
Requirement Rationale: Operational Interface

Summary: CF: Freeze Channel Command
Description: When CF receives a "Freeze Channel" command, CF shall disable the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface that halts all transactions at their current state. (timers, suspend, etc.) Typically used for contact scheduling

Summary: CF: Freeze Channel Command - Pause In-Progress Transactions
Description: When CF receives a "Freeze Channel" command, CF shall pause all in-progress transactions for the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure command is applied immediately

Summary: CF: Freeze Channel Command - New Transaction While Frozen
Description: While a channel is frozen, when a new transaction is received for that channel, CF shall not process that transaction.
Requirement Rationale: A frozen channel cannot receive new transactions

Summary: CF: Thaw Channel Command
Description: When CF receives a "Thaw Channel" command, CF shall re-enable the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Operational Interface

Summary: CF: Thaw Channel Command - Resume Paused Transactions
Description: When CF receives a "Thaw Channel" command, CF shall resume processing all paused transactions for the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface that resumes all transactions at their current state. (timers, suspend,…) Typical used for contact scheduling

Summary: CF: Commandable Protocol Parameters
Description:
The following parameters shall be configurable by a CF command:
1. CFDP channel Ack-Timer Value (seconds)
2. CFDP channel NAK-Timer Value (seconds)  
3. CFDP channel Inactivity-Timeout Value (seconds) 
4. CFDP channel Maximum Ack Timeouts (integer counts)
5. CFDP channel Maximum NAK Timeouts (integer counts)
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to support mission variability and reconfiguration

Summary: CF: Commandable Protocol Parameters - Configuration Table Defaults
Description:
The default values for the CFDP channel protocol parameters below shall be defined by a CF Configuration Table:
1. CFDP channel Ack-Timer Value (seconds)
2. CFDP channel NAK-Timer Value (seconds)  
3. CFDP channel Inactivity-Timeout Value (seconds) 
4. CFDP channel Maximum Ack Timeouts (integer counts)
5. CFDP channel Maximum NAK Timeouts (integer counts)
Requirement Rationale: Ensure CF starts in a known and valid operational state

Summary: CF: Set Protocol Configuration Command
Description: When CF receives a "Set CFDP Channel Protocol Configuration" command, CF shall set the command-specified parameter to the command-specified value and issue a cFE event message that confirms the change.
Requirement Rationale: Operational Interface

Summary: CF: Set Protocol Configuration Command - Invalid Parameter
Description: When CF receives a "Set CFDP Channel Protocol Configuration" command,  if the command-specified parameter is invalid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Command validity check for robust operation

Summary: CF: Set Protocol Configuration Command - Invalid Parameter Value
Description: When CF receives a "Set CFDP Channel Protocol Configuration" command,  if the command-specified parameter *value* is invalid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Command validity check for robust operation

Summary: CF: Get Protocol Configuration Command
Description: When CF receives a "Get CFDP Channel-Protocol Configuration Parameter" command, CF shall issue an event message containing the current value of the command-specified configuration-table parameter.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface

Summary: CF: Get Protocol Configuration Command - Invalid Parameter
Description: When CF receives a "Get CFDP Channel-Protocol Configuration Parameter" command, if the command-specified parameter is invalid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Operational robustness

Summary: CF: Cancel Transaction Command
Description: When CF receives a "Cancel Transaction" command, CF shall cancel the transaction indicated by the command-specified Entity ID and transaction-sequence number.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to control transactions. Transaction-Id provides a mechanism to scale to large systems and avoid performance issues with string searches

Summary: CF: Cancel Transaction Command - Transaction Not In Progress
Description: When CF receives a "Cancel Transaction" command, if the command-specified transaction is not in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Abandon Transaction Command
Description: When CF receives an "Abandon Transaction" command, CF shall abandon the command-specified transaction.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Abandon Transaction Command - Transaction Not In Progress
Description: When CF receives an "Abandon Transaction" command, if the command-specified transaction is not in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Abandon All Transactions Command
Description: When CF receives an "Abandon All Transactions" command, CF shall abandon all transactions.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface that removes transaction state for all active transaction.

Summary: CF: Abandon All Transactions Command - No Transactions In Progress
Description: When CF receives an "Abandon All Transactions" command, if there are no transactions in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Write Active Transactions Command
Description: When CF receives a "Write Active Transactions" command, CF shall write all active transactions to a file.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface supporting operator insight into transfer sequence and state

Summary: CF: Enable Dequeue Command
Description: When CF receives an "Enable Dequeue" command, CF shall enable the dequeueing of pending transactions for the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface that allows queued file transfers to begin on a channel. Separate from channel freeze so that transfer requests can continue to be queued while transmission is withheld.

Summary: CF: Enable Dequeue Command - Invalid Channel
Description: When CF receives an "Enable Dequeue" command, if the command-specified channel is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Disable Dequeue Command
Description: When CF receives a "Disable Dequeue" command, CF shall disable the dequeueing of pending transactions for the command-specified channel.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface that withholds pending file transfers from becoming active while allowing in-progress transactions to complete. Typically used to quiesce a channel before reconfiguration.

Summary: CF: Disable Dequeue Command - Invalid Channel
Description: When CF receives a "Disable Dequeue" command, if the command-specified channel is not valid, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Maximum Simultaneous Transactions Per Channel
Description: The CF maximum number of simultaneous per-channel transactions shall be defined and configured at compile time.
Requirement Rationale: Channel concept extended to allow independent operations when other channels may be blocked due to maximum transactions

Summary: CF: Maximum Downlink PDU Size Per Channel
Description: The CF maximum per-channel downlink-PDU size shall be defined and configured at compile time.
Requirement Rationale: Support constraints for security checks and resource utilization. Allows the PDU size to be optimized for the channel communications stack (MTU for transport and data link)

Summary: CF: Cancel All Transactions Command
Description: When CF receives a "Cancel All Transactions" command, CF shall cancel all in-progress transactions.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to control transactions.  "All" provides an interface to cancel transactions without having knowledge of each individual transaction number. Especially useful when there may be hundreds or thousands of transactions in progress.

Summary: CF: Cancel All Transactions Command - No Transactions In Progress
Description: When CF receives "Cancel *All* Transactions" command, if there are no transactions in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Suspend Transaction Command
Description: When CF receives a "Suspend Transaction" command, if the command-specified transaction is not in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Suspend Transaction Command - Transaction Not In Progress
Description: When CF receives a "Suspend Transaction" command, if the command-specified transaction is not in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Suspend All Transactions Command
Description: When CF receives a "Suspend All Transactions" command, CF shall suspend all in-progress transactions.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to align file transfer with communications contact schedule.

Summary: CF: Suspend All Transactions Command - No Transactions In Progress
Description: When CF receives a "Suspend All Transactions" command, if no transactions are in progress, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Resume Transaction Command
Description: When CF receives a "Resume Transaction" command, CF shall resume the command-specified suspended transaction
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to resume normal operations without knowing which files are suspended

Summary: CF: Resume Transaction Command - Transaction Not Suspended
Description: When CF receives a "Resume Transaction" command, if the command-specified transaction is not suspended, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface

Summary: CF: Resume All Transactions Command
Description: When CF receives a "Resume *All* Transactions", CF shall resume all suspended transactions
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to resume normal operations without knowing which files are suspended

Summary: CF: Resume All Transactions Command - No Suspended Transactions
Description: When CF receives a "Resume ALL Transactions", if there are no suspended transactions, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Purge Queue Command
Description: When CF receives a "Purge Queue" command, CF shall purge the command-specified queue for the command-specified output channel.
Requirement Rationale: Support an operational interface to provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Purge Queue Command - Undefined Queue
Description: When CF receives a "Purge Queue" command, if the command-specified queue is not defined, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Purge Queue Command - Undefined Channel
Description: When CF receives a "Purge Queue" command, if the command-specified channel is not defined, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Write Queue Command
Description: When CF receives a "Write Queue" command, CF shall write the command-specified queue's contents to the command-specified file.
Requirement Rationale: Operational interface to allow insight into file transfer order.

Summary: CF: Write Queue Command - Undefined Queue
Description: When CF receives a "Write Queue" command, if the command-specified queue is not defined, CF shall reject the command.
Requirement Rationale: Ensure robust operations and provide operator feedback.

Summary: CF: Maximum Simultaneous Transactions
Description: The maximum number of transmissions, that is, the sum of simultaneous transmit and receive transactions, shall be defined at compile time.
Requirement Rationale: Supports scaling resource use for mission variability

Summary: CF: Maximum Transferable File Size
Description: When CF receives a file-transfer request, if the requested file's size is larger than 2^32 bytes, CF shall reject the request and issue an error event message.
Requirement Rationale: Constrain resources use and exclude implementation complexity of CCSDS  Large-file-size header extensions. CFDP-1S-01

Summary: CF: Entity ID Field Size Limit
Description: When CF receives a PDU, if the size of the Entity ID fields are too large for the configured internal storage, CF shall reject the PDU and issue an error event message.
Requirement Rationale: Prevent silent truncation of variable length Entity ID fields in PDU by checking the configured storage size and rejecting PDUs that with an Entity ID field that would be truncated.

Summary: CF: Transaction Sequence Number Field Size Limit
Description: When CF receives a PDU, if the size of the Transaction Sequence Number field is too large for the configured internal storage, CF shall reject the PDU and issue an error event message.
Requirement Rationale: Prevent silent truncation of variable length Transaction Sequence Number field in PDU by checking configured storage size and rejecting PDUs that with a Transaction Sequence Number field that would be truncated.

Summary: CF: File Transfer Priority Levels
Description: Each CF output channel shall have 256 file-transfer priority levels.
Requirement Rationale: Priority levels are used to control the order of file transfer PDUs within a channel. Priority levels allow the control of PDU interleaving in a output channel and prevent a lower-priority transfer from blocking a high-priority operational transfer. 256 priority levels provide a high-level of granularity in the compact space of 1 byte.

Summary: CF: File Transfer Priority Levels - Configurable Polling Directory Priority
Description: The CF file transmission priority level for each polling directory shall be configurable.
Requirement Rationale: Supports management of priorities for each polling directory.  Commanded transfers (single file or playback directory) use the priority level contained in the command.

Summary: CF: File Transfer Priority Levels - Highest Priority Value
Description: The highest file-transfer priority level shall be zero.
Requirement Rationale: Standardized interface. If the number of levels increases or decreases the highest priority will always be the same

Summary: CF: NAK Retransmission Ordering
Description: CF shall send NAK re-transmissions in the order received at the same priority as the NAK-targeted file
Requirement Rationale: PDU re-transmission priority should be the same as the original request. To not do so would allow a form of priority inversion where a large number of NAKs on a lower priority transfer would suppress re-transmission of higher priority transfers.

Summary: CF: Class 1 Unacknowledged Service
Description: CF shall support CFDP file transfers in "Unacknowledged"(Class-1) Service Mode.
Requirement Rationale: Basic file transfer function. Unacknowledged Mode, also called unreliable mode, is used for non-critical data or operations without bi-directional data paths.

Summary: CF: Class 2 Acknowledged Service
Description: CF shall support CFDP file transfer in "Acknowledged" (Class-2) Service, Mode.
Requirement Rationale: Basic file transfer function. Acknowledged Mode, also called reliable mode, is used for critical data and/or operations with bi-directional data paths.

Summary: CF: Housekeeping Message
Description:
The CF Housekeeping message shall include
1. Command Counter
2. Command Error Counter
-- Per-Channel HouseKeeping Entries
3. Number of transactions on the various queues
4. Number of active polling directories
5. Number of active playback directories
6. Frozen Status
7. Number of Sent File Data Bytes
8. Number of Sent PDUs
9. Number of Sent NAK Segment Requests
10. Number of Received File Data Bytes
11. Number of Received PDUs with Valid Headers
12. Number of Received PDUs with Errors
13. Number of Spurious Received PDUs
14. Number of Dropped Received PDUs
15. Number of Received NAK Segment Requests
16. Number of File Open Faults
17. Number of File Read Faults
18. Number of File Seek Faults
19. Number of File Write Faults
20. Number of File Rename Faults
21. Number of Directory Read Faults
22. Number of CRC Mismatch Faults
23. Number of File Size Mismatch Faults
24. Number of NAK Limit Exceeded Faults
25. Number of ACK Limit Exceeded Faults
26. Number of Inactivity Timer Limit Exceeded Faults
Requirement Rationale: Operator interface that provides detailed status on operational state

Summary: CF: End Of Transaction Message
Description:
The CF End of Transaction message shall include
1. Transaction identifier
2. Channel number
3. Direction of transaction
4. Filenames associated with transaction
5. Transaction state
6. Condition code
7. Source EID of transaction
8. Peer EID of transaction
9. File size
10. CRC state
Requirement Rationale: Operator interface that provides detailed information on transaction

Summary: CF: End Of Transaction Message - Generation
Description: When a transaction terminates, CF shall generate an End of Transaction information packet
Requirement Rationale: Operational awareness of transaction closure and potential automation of follow-on actions

Summary: CF: End Of Transaction Message - Condition Code On Normal Completion
Description: If a transaction has reached the FIN or EOF state, the CF End of Transaction message Condition Code shall be set to the CFDP condition code for that transaction.
Requirement Rationale: Preserves the CFDP transaction result in telemetry for operator assessment and automated processing

Summary: CF: End Of Transaction Message - Condition Code On Early Termination
Description: If the transaction has not reached the FIN or EOF state, the CF End of Transaction message Condition Code shall indicate why the transaction stopped early.
Requirement Rationale: Provides the cause of premature transaction termination in telemetry to support fault diagnosis and recovery

Summary: CF: Initialize Housekeeping Data
Description: When CF is initialized, CF shall initialize the the housekeeping counters/numbers to zero and the frozen status as "thawed".
Requirement Rationale: All variable must be set to a known valid state on initialization to support reliable functioning

Summary: CF: Load Configuration Tables
Description: When CF is initialized, CF shall load valid CF Configuration Tables.
Requirement Rationale: All variables must be set to a known valid state on initialization to support reliable functioning. Table interface supports operational reconfiguration of CF functions.

Summary: CF: Load Configuration Tables - Validation Failure
Description: If a CF Configuration Table fails validation, CF shall issue an error cFE event message and exit.
Requirement Rationale: Support constraints for security checks and resource utilization. Without a valid configuration CF can not initialize to a functional state.

Summary: CF: Load Configuration Tables - Parameter Validation
Description: CF shall validate CF configuration table parameters.
Requirement Rationale: Support constraints for security checks and resource utilization. Without a valid configuration CF can not initialize to a functional state.  Specific content validation is implementation defined.

Summary: CF: Enable Engine Command
Description: When CF receives an "Initialize Engine" command, CF shall enable the CFDP engine and re-load its configuration.
Requirement Rationale: Supports operator interface to disable operations due to misconfiguration and other faults

Summary: CF: Disable Engine Command
Description: When CF receives a "Disable Engine" command, CF shall disable the CFDP engine and reset its state.
Requirement Rationale: Supports operator interface to disable operations due to misconfiguration and other faults
